findings.title: Test named "wrong docType is still caught" asserts nothing is caught
findings.description: The test `a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic` makes three `validateFrontmatter` calls and all three expect `toHaveLength(0)`. None of them exercises a failing docType constraint. The first two inputs are valid devlog and gate-evidence documents. The third is an unknown docType, which `validateFrontmatter` passes through unvalidated (`frontmatterSchema.ts` step 2, `if (!schema) return findings`). The name and the comments ("proves the values constraint ... is enforced") contradict what the assertions show. The test gives false confidence and duplicates the "validates clean" tests above it. Delete it. Or, if the intent is to cover the `values` constraint, add a case that produces a finding. For example, make `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS['devlog'].fields.docType.values` the thing under test, or assert it equals `['devlog']`.

findings.title: Test file leaks spies and `process.exitCode` across tests
findings.description: `beforeEach` calls `vi.clearAllMocks()`. That clears call history but does not restore spies. The `process.exit` spy installed in the "exits 2" test (line 87) keeps its no-op implementation for any later test. The `console` and `process.stdout.write` spies are never restored. Tests that set `process.exitCode = 1` leave it set after the file finishes, and only the next `beforeEach` resets it. The last test in the file happens to leave it unset, so the suite works today, but it depends on test order, which the testing rules say to avoid. Add an `afterEach` with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` and `process.exitCode = undefined`. Also, no test covers the other operational-error path to exit code 2, the missing `projectPath` `UserError`.

findings.title: `validateFrontmatterAction` is too long and mixes fix, report and exit-code concerns
findings.description: The function is about 70 lines, over the project's ~50 line guideline. It resolves the project, runs validation, applies fixes, builds JSON output and sets the exit code. The fix loop (lines 109-134) is self-contained and could move to something like `applyFixes(findings): { fixLog, fixErrors, remaining }`. The action would then read as resolve, validate, fix, report, exit. `FixLogRecord` (lines 26-31) also restates a subset of core's `FixLogEntry`, which `updateFrontmatterField` already returns. Reuse that type instead of keeping a parallel shape.

findings.title: Duplicated severity table and a silent `'?'` fallback
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON` is a copy of the table in `check.ts:25-29`, minus `info`. It is typed `Record<string, string>`, and the call site (line 62) uses `?? '?'`. `FrontmatterFinding.severity` is the closed union `'warning' | 'error'`. Typing the table as `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>` makes the fallback unnecessary, and the compiler would flag a missing severity. That fits the project rule against silent fallback values. Better still, share one table between `check.ts` and `validate.ts`. The icon and colour selection is also written twice (here and in `formatFinding` in `check.ts`).

findings.title: Exit codes are bare literals with no documented contract
findings.description: The command uses exit code 1 for "findings remain" (`process.exitCode = 1`, line 155). It uses 2 for operational errors (`handleError(err, 2)`, line 180). The meanings exist only as scattered numeric literals. This command is described as meant for scripts, yet neither the `--help` text nor a constant records them. The rest of the CLI uses exit 1 for operational errors, so callers get a different meaning for the same code depending on the command. Define named constants (for example `EXIT_FINDINGS` and `EXIT_ERROR`) next to `handleError`. Mention the codes in the command description. `errors.ts:46` is fine as written: `exitCode = 1` is the existing behaviour and not a new magic default.

findings.title: JSON output is built as `Record<string, unknown>` and omits the post-fix outcome
findings.description: The JSON output is a scripted-consumer contract, but it is typed `Record<string, unknown>`. Declare an interface for it. The counts (`totalFindings`, `errors`, `warnings`) are computed from the pre-fix `findings`. The exit code, however, is driven by `remaining`, and `remaining` is not in the JSON. A consumer using `--fix --json` has to derive "did it pass" from `totalFindings`, `fixed` and `fixErrors`. Emitting a `remaining` count would make the JSON agree with the exit status.

findings.title: Explicit paths that don't match are silently skipped, so a typo gives a clean exit 0
findings.description: This follows the documented design of `resolveExplicitPaths` (a staged-file list legitimately contains deletions and non-markdown files). A mistyped or out-of-root path therefore reports "No inconsistencies found (0 files checked)" and exits 0. Used as a gate in a script, that is a false pass. The `--help` text does say others are silently skipped. Consider at least a stderr note when paths were given but `filesChecked` is 0, or when some given paths were dropped.

findings.title: Machine-artifact docType schemas and the `dateUpdated` omission
findings.description: The three new schemas (`review-resolution`, `gate-evidence`, `devlog`) require only `docType` and `dateCreated`. The comment explaining why `dateUpdated` is excluded matches the code. I checked `validateFrontmatter` and none of these schemas can produce a `fixAction`: `dateCreated` has no inference path and there is no `status` field. So `--fix` cannot reach `updateFrontmatterField`, which always stamps `dateUpdated` (`markdownWriter.ts:138-140`), for these docTypes. The existing schema tests were correctly narrowed to `EXPECTED_DOC_TYPES` so they no longer require `status` or `dateUpdated` of the new types.

findings.title: Command wiring and error handling follow existing conventions
findings.description: The command follows the shape of `check.ts`: it uses `withJsonOption`, `withProjectOption` and `withFixOption`, resolves the project through `resolveProjectWorktree`, and sends errors through `handleError`. `validateFrontmatterFiles` and `updateFrontmatterField` are both exported from `core/node` (`node.ts:23,40`). Per-fix failures are caught, narrowed with `instanceof Error`, recorded in `fixErrors`, and reflected in the exit code, so nothing is swallowed. The tests cover the clean, findings, fix-success, fix-failure, unfixable, JSON and path-forwarding cases, and they check that `dateUpdated` is stamped through the fourth argument.
